Rotate a point about a centre The same process, now with any angle Subtract C Rotate about zero Add C For any angle, how do the two legs of Q determine Q'? 90-degree check retained: Q'=(-v,u), giving P'=(1,3).
Rotate a point about a centre Inside the rotation: follow the horizontal leg Q=(u,v) from subtracting C  ->  Rotate about zero  ->  Q'
Rotate a point about a centre Inside the rotation: turn the other leg and join Same Q=(u,v): retain H and turn the remaining vertical leg.
Rotate a point about a centre Return: put the result into the same middle operation Subtract C Rotate about zero Add C Negative u or v: reverse the leg. Zero: omit it. Positive theta: CCW.
Rotate a point about a centre Use it: the same P and C, now 30 degrees

Rotate a point about a centre Subtract the centre. Turn the offset. Add it back. Subtract C Rotate about zero Add C Equal axis scales. Positive theta: counterclockwise; negative: clockwise. Checks: C stays fixed; distance to C stays fixed; zero turn gives P.
